sample.conflict: Main-results section 3.2.2 says 9341 men; Figure 2 caption says 9583. Supplement unavailable; no reconciliation inferred. Joint-cell n not extracted.

measurement.fasting: Nonfasting collection; self-reported elapsed time in hourly categories; 7+ hours treated as fasting reference

analysis.outcome_scale: log(TG); coefficients back-transformed to relative differences
analysis.exposures: 15 combinations of age [40-49,50-59,60-69,70-79,80+] and BMI [<25,25-29.9,>=30]; sex-specific models
analysis.caution: Figure 2 caption identifies education and lipid-lowering medication as women-only in that plot; exact final Figure 3/table covariate implementation needs supplement confirmation.

unretrieved_statistics.description: 28 nonreference sex-specific age-by-BMI adjusted back-transformed log-TG ratios and 95% CI
unretrieved_statistics.claimed_location: Supplementary Table 1; Figure 3 shows estimates graphically
unretrieved_statistics.status: NOT EXTRACTED; no numerical digitization performed

interpretation_limits: A test P value does not provide interaction magnitude or sign. P=0.32 does not establish zero interaction.
Back-transformed log coefficients are conditional relative effects, not unadjusted arithmetic means.
Nonfasting-to-fasting transport is an assumption; time adjustment alone does not identify fasting target subgroup means. Dropped interactions after significance screening do not prove absence.
Age 80+ is outside the parent-provided prospective 40-79 target range. Underweight and normal BMI are combined.
Shared reference induces covariance between joint-category estimates; marginal CIs alone are insufficient for new pairwise-contrast uncertainty.
Cross-sectional selection and unmeasured covariates limit transport; no target observations examined.

sources.citation: Zhang Y, Pei Y, Yan Y, et al. Chinese Population-Wide Lipid Trajectories From Age 20 to 85 Years: Sex- and Adiposity-Specific Patterns. JACC Asia. Published March 6, 2026.
sources.cohort: China-PAR; China MUCA 1998, InterASIA 2000-2001, CIMIC 2007-2008; follow-ups through 2018-2021
sources.design: Longitudinal cohort; repeated lipids and time-varying BMI; sex-specific linear mixed-effects models
sources.population: Chinese adults enrolled age >=18; excluded baseline myocardial infarction, stroke, heart failure, cancer; missing baseline or all follow-up lipids

measurement.laboratory: Participated in CDC Lipid Standardization Program; exact TG instrument/reagent not given in extracted main-text methods
measurement.bmi: Measured height and weight; z-score exposure; exact SD normalization denominator not established

analysis.outcome_scale: Raw TG mg/dL in Tables 2 and 3; separate log-TG sensitivity table not retrieved
analysis.effect_unit: mg/dL TG per 1-SD increase in BMI
analysis.age_split: Before versus after TG crossing age 54 years; equality convention not specified in extracted table; crossing estimated where sex-specific trajectories meet
analysis.standardization: No conversion to mg/dL per kg/m^2; baseline sex-specific BMI SD is not assumed equal to model standardization SD

interpretation_limits: These are adjusted repeated-measure associations, not causal effects or pure within-person changes.
Before/after age-54 strata extend beyond 40-79; transfer to a restricted target age range is not guaranteed.
Table 3 Pinteraction column compares sexes, whereas superscript c denotes age interaction P<0.05.
No joint subgroup intercepts, residual variances, coefficient covariance matrix, or exact standardized-BMI denominator extracted.
Waist-circumference trajectories in Figure 2 are not BMI evidence; no WC-to-BMI substitution.
Main paper reports log-TG sensitivity in Supplemental Table 10 and BMI-group curves in Supplemental Figure 12; neither retrieved.
China-PAR subcohorts and tables overlap; do not treat repeated statistics as independent cohorts.
